body:
> Doesn't happen if CursorLine has a fg color (eg. guifg=#ff0000), 

Because then CursorLine is "high priority". Otherwise it's "low priority".

> although in practice you probably don't ever want to assign a fg color to CursorLine.

If your DiffChange/DiffAdd has a bg color, then before #9028 was implemented, `CursorLine` would be unreadable for foreground text that did not highly contrast the DiffChange/DiffAdd bg color. Now it's always readable, but the tradeoff is that it shows a underline.

I guess now we need a `CursorLineDiff` highlight group as promised in https://github.com/neovim/neovim/pull/9028#discussion_r236479290

From the useless eyecandy department.

```
let x = nvim_open_win(0, v:true, {'relative': 'editor', 'row': 4, 'col': 4, 'width': 30, 'height': 3})
set floatblend=20 " window local option
 ```

Blending can additionally be overriden per highlight group (inside a float). This works:

```
hi PmenuSel blend=0
```

To disable blending of current item when `pumblend` is otherwise active.

issue.body:
### Neovim version (nvim -v)

0.5.1

### Vim (not Nvim) behaves the same?

no, vim 8.2.344

Linux, 5.10.70-1-MANJARO

urxvt, 9.22

screen-256color

Arch User Repository (AUR)

### How to reproduce the issue

```sh
nvim --clean -d \
    +"windo set cul nu" \
    +"hi CursorLine term=none cterm=none ctermbg=blue" \
    <(echo -e "lorem\nipsum\ndolor sit\namet\n\n") \
    <(echo -e "lorem\nipsum\ndolor sores\nerratum\n\n")
```
1. notice how line `1` has background and no underline
1. go to line `3` or `4`
1. notice extra underline and ignored background setting
1. `:set nocul`
1. notice disabling cursor line hides underline in the left window
1. `:hi CursorLine ctermfg=white`
1. notice no underline and proper background in the right window (but no diff highlighting)
1. `:hi CursorLine ctermfg=none`
1. notice how cursor line in the right window is broken again (but diff is highlighted)

### Expected behavior

Cursor line in diff mode should adhere to `CursorLine` settings, i.e. have correct decorations and background even when foreground colour is not set (mind that difference between `sit` and `sores` in that line should be highlighted as well):

Cursor line decorations and background colour settings overloaded when foreground colour is not set:

issue.title: Cursorline has underline when current line is on a diff

repository.name: diffview.nvim
repository.description: Single tabpage interface for easily cycling through diffs for all modified files for any git rev.

issue.body:
I am using [onedark](https://github.com/navarasu/onedark.nvim) colorscheme, and diffview with `enhanced_diff_hl` set

```
  vim.opt.fillchars = { diff = " " }

  require('diffview').setup({
    enhanced_diff_hl = true,
  })
```

In the below screenshot you can see my current line is 438, and the cursorline is displayed as a slightly lighter gray background

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/6157939/151146828-0685f3ad-6426-4ab8-909e-645a14af0bfc.png)

However, when I move the cursor over a diff (in this case my current line is 443, within some *added* lines), the cursorline now includes an underscore.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/6157939/151147071-3b369985-b9ac-479d-bf03-2646a7df8238.png)

The only highlight I can see referencing Cursorline is the following:

```
DiffviewCursorLine xxx guibg=#31353f
	Last set from ~/.local/share/nvim/site/pack/packer/start/onedark.nvim/colors/onedark.lua
``

However, modifying `DiffviewCursorLine` only affects the file_browser tab, not the diff view of the source code itself.

If I attempt to get the numeric syntax ID when the cursor is within a diff (`synID(line('.'), col('.'), 1)`), it just returns 0, which isn't helpful in finding the syntax group.

Do you have any idea where this underline is coming from, and how to disable it?
